message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment.  
If you’d like up‑to‑date information, you can check one of the following resources:

| Service | How to use |
|---------|------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and view the current AQI, pollutant levels, and health recommendations. |
| **OpenAQ** | Go to https://openaq.org/, search for “Los Angeles”, and look at the latest measurements for PM₂.₅, NO₂, O₃, etc. |
| **Weather.com / AccuWeather** | Many weather sites include an AQI widget for major cities. |
| **Mobile Apps** | Apps like “AirVisual”, “Plume Labs: Air Report”, or the EPA’s own “AirNow” app provide real‑time alerts. |

If you’re interested in historical trends or want to pull the data programmatically, you can use the AirNow API (requires a free API key) or the OpenAQ API. Let me know if you’d like a quick example of how to query one of those APIs!
